approach: Add `pub fn check_request_coverage(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and call it from `check_reading_acceptance` right after `check_criteria_evidence`. That function is the one gate that `read_for` (first attempt and retry) and `check_reading_text` (replay and `athena check-reading`) both run. The check parses the request into parts: `(N)` markers in sequence from (1), and the bullets under an `Acceptance:` heading. It refuses a reading when a part has no covering criterion, or when an out_of_scope item defers it. Coverage is word overlap, not meaning. A request that itself defers the part is exempt. A request with no parts or bullets is unaffected. The doc comment names the root cause, cites jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, and carries the 'refuses more readings' sentence. Unit tests, a CHANGELOG entry and a one-line sixth READING_RULES line in briefs.rs (a Rust const, not a budgeted prompt file) complete it. Revision: criteria 6 and 7 now state what fails without the behavior.

decisions.choice: Put the check in reading.rs as a new function called from check_reading_acceptance, after check_criteria_evidence, and skip readings with no capability, with a question, or with no deliverables, as check_governance_coverage does.
decisions.reason: check_reading_acceptance is the single gate used by Athena::read_for (including the retry read) and by check_reading_text (replay and check-reading). The fault is that this gate never compares the request's parts with the reading, so fixing it here covers the whole class.

rejected.option: Edit reader or verifier prompts to say 'do not defer named parts'
rejected.why: Prose only; the reader budget has 3 tokens of headroom and the mechanism default requires a code check.

rejected.option: Check at verification time, when the verifier sees the diff
rejected.why: Too late: the producer has already run on a narrowed scope. The reading gate can still send the refusal back to the reader.

decisions.choice: Parts are `(N)` markers read in sequence from (1) (at least two, so a lone '(1)' is ignored), and bullets under an `Acceptance:` line that end at the first blank or non-bullet line. A part's text runs to the next marker or the end of the paragraph. Reuse `is_bullet`.
decisions.reason: This matches the request shapes seen: inline '(1) ... (2) ... (3)' and the `Acceptance:` section. Bullets outside an Acceptance heading are not parts, so ordinary lists cause no false refusals.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet or numbered line of a request as a part
rejected.why: Wider than the incident class and more false refusals; the request-format fact ties bullets to acceptance only.

rejected.option: Use a model to compare parts and criteria
rejected.why: Costs a call and is not deterministic; the other reading checks cost no model call.

decisions.choice: A part is covered when one criterion shares min(2, n) distinctive words with it (n = distinctive words in the part). A distinctive word has 5+ letters, is lowercased, loses a trailing ing/ed/es/s, and is not in a small stop list. A criterion naming '(N)' or 'part N' also covers part N. A part with no distinctive words is skipped.
decisions.reason: Deterministic and lenient, tuned toward few false refusals. Two shared words stop a generic word like 'change' from covering everything.

rejected.option: Require the bullet text verbatim in a criterion
rejected.why: The reader legitimately rewords; verbatim matching would refuse correct readings.
'change', 'tests' and similar words would cover any part.

decisions.choice: A part is deferred when an out_of_scope item names it as 'part (N)', '(N)' or 'part N', or shares min(2, n) distinctive words with it and also holds a deferral phrase (follow-up, follow up, later job, later request, separate request, separate job, next job, another job, defer). Deferral refuses even if a criterion covers the part. A part whose own text, or another request sentence naming it, holds a deferral phrase, 'out of scope' or 'not in this job' is exempt.
decisions.reason: The rule: explicit parts are in scope unless the user defers them. Naming the part number in out_of_scope is always a drop. Word overlap alone needs a deferral phrase, so ordinary exclusions stay legal.

rejected.option: Refuse any out_of_scope item that shares words with a part
rejected.why: Would refuse legitimate narrowing such as 'files of job X stay as landed'.

decisions.choice: The refusal error names each problem by part label and text and states the repair: add a criterion, remove it from out_of_scope, or have the request itself defer it. Deliverables are not text-compared.
decisions.reason: The reader gets one immediate re-read with the refusal text. A Deliverable has only a path, so no reliable text mapping exists.

rejected.option: Also require a deliverable per part
rejected.why: Deliverables carry only paths; the comparison would be guesswork and refuse correct readings.

rejected.why: The reader would learn of the check only from a refusal, costing a read, and the brief's own test requires each reading check to have a rule line.

risks.risk: Word-overlap coverage is heuristic: it may wrongly refuse a reworded reading or accept one that only mentions the words.
risks.mitigation: Require only min(2, n) shared words after a stop list, accept a criterion that names '(N)', keep the exemption phrases, and include a reworded-but-covered test. The error says what to add and the reader gets one re-read.

risks.risk: Steward and Hestia requests carry an Acceptance: section, so every such job is now checked; a fake reader in an integration test could be refused.
risks.mitigation: Run cargo test --locked. If a fixture fails, give its reading a matching criterion rather than loosening the check.

risks.risk: The new doc comment must keep the structure the existing source-reading tests expect; a stray 'pub fn check_request_coverage' string earlier in the file would break the split.
risks.mitigation: Place the function before the tests module, write the intended-refusal paragraph last in the doc, and use that literal once outside test code.

risks.risk: The sixth rule line could break the briefs.rs rule-section test (220 bytes per line, 2400 bytes per section).
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 190 bytes; run cargo test -p athena-context; shorten the line rather than raise a cap.

risks.risk: The parser finds '(1)' in ordinary prose such as 'time(s)' or footnotes and invents parts.
risks.mitigation: Require sequential markers from (1) with at least two, and test a request with one lone '(1)'.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in the reading.rs tests module calling the production gate `check_reading_acceptance(&reading, request, None, &[], None)`. Preconditions: reading.capability is Some, question is None, deliverables non-empty. The reading comes from the existing `scoped_reading` helper (line ~4992), with criteria covering parts (1) and (2) but not (3) and out_of_scope holding 'Part (3) is deferred to a follow-up request'. The request is the text of job 20261029-084645-sza7 with parts (1), (2), (3), a plain string argument. Records are absent from the snapshot, so the producer reconstructs the text from the brief and says so in a comment. No double: the helper and `Reading` exist today.
demonstrations.observes: check_reading_acceptance returns Err whose message contains '(3)'. The same reading with the out_of_scope item removed and a criterion for (3) added returns Ok.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without check_request_coverage, check_reading_acceptance returns Ok for this reading, so the unwrap_err assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Two tests through `check_reading_acceptance` with `scoped_reading` and replaced criteria. (a) A request with parts (1) (2) (3) and a reading whose criteria cover only (1) and (2), with no out_of_scope mention of (3), is refused. (b) The same request with a criterion per part and a deliverable is accepted. The seam, `scoped_reading`, exists today.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the coverage check, (a) is accepted and its is_err assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Tests through `check_reading_acceptance`. (a) A request saying '(3) is a follow-up, not part of this job' or 'Part (3) is out of scope', with a reading whose out_of_scope defers (3) and no criterion for it, is accepted. (b) An Acceptance bullet containing 'later' or 'follow-up' is exempt. (c) Requests with no numbered parts and no Acceptance heading ('add a greeting', and a request with a plain '- ' list outside Acceptance, and a lone '(1)') are unaffected. (d) The existing reading tests stay green; their helper requests hold no parts.
demonstrations.observes: (a)-(c) return Ok(()); the whole existing reading test module passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the request exception were missing, (a) would be refused and fail. If the parser took every list line as a part, (c) would fail.

Acceptance:

demonstrations.method: Source-text test in the reading.rs tests module, in the style of `prior_result_refusal_is_declared_intended` (line ~5529). It uses `include_str!("reading.rs")`, takes the doc paragraphs before `pub fn check_request_coverage`, and checks they hold the root-cause wording (no comparison of the request's named parts with the reading) and both job ids. It also checks that the body of `check_reading_acceptance` contains the call `check_request_coverage(reading, request)`. A Grep of reading.rs gives the same evidence.
demonstrations.observes: The doc comment holds both ids and the root-cause sentence, and the call site exists in check_reading_acceptance.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the function, its doc comment or the call in check_reading_acceptance were missing, the include_str test fails (the doc split finds no function, or the call string is absent).

demonstrations.method: Two parts. (i) A source-and-changelog test in the style of line ~5529: `replay_declaration` of a criterion with 'expected 5% of newly refused readings' gives share Some(5); the check's last doc paragraph holds 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.'; CHANGELOG.md holds the phrase. (ii) The full athena-core suite runs the existing replay and acceptance tests (`replay_case`, `base_checker`, `marker_candidate` and earlier acceptance tests) unchanged against the new gate; they pass real-shaped requests and readings through `check_reading_acceptance`. The replay corpus lives in records/ and is absent from the snapshot, so the 5% is an estimate, not a measurement, and the doc comment says so. Seams exist today.
demonstrations.observes: The declared share parses as 5, the doc and changelog carry the intended-refusal sentence, and every existing replay and acceptance test still passes, so past accepted readings are not refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the intended-refusal declaration were missing, the declaration test fails (no share parsed or no sentence in the doc). If the new check were too strict and refused past readings, the existing replay and acceptance tests fail. If the check were absent, the part-(3) test of criterion 1 in the same run fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the three gates over the workspace as one chain. They exercise the briefs.rs rule-section test with 6 rules (220-byte per-line and 2400-byte section caps), `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (budgets unchanged) and every new test. No double or seam: this is the real toolchain on the real tree.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the change's own consistency the chain fails. If READING_RULES gains a sixth line but the array size or the check list in the rule-section test is not updated, `cargo test` fails. If the new helpers are left unused or badly formatted, clippy (dead_code, -D warnings) or fmt fails. If the check refuses a fixture reading, `cargo test` fails.
